Akara raises $5.5 million for hospital sensors and operational AI

Trinity College Dublin spinout Akara raised $5.5 million led by Locke Health, bringing total funding to $12.3 million. Its sensors, AI agents and robotics aim to reduce documentation and coordinate clinical-space use.

GlobeNewswire / Akara ↗11 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

Funding for hospital operations

Trinity College Dublin spinout Akara raised $5.5 million led by Locke Health, bringing total funding to $12.3 million. Its sensors, AI agents and robotics aim to reduce documentation and coordinate clinical-space use.

Thermal activity sensing

Wall-mounted sensors combine thermal sensing and on-device AI to detect activity without conventional detailed patient imagery. Software alerts staff when needed and supports natural-language questions and reports. Akara sees that information as a foundation for further automation.

Expansion rather than a new robot

Akara reports use in U.S. hospitals and ambulatory surgery centers. Funding will expand engineering and operations and develop AI agents. This is not a new robot launch or a quantified savings result transferable to every hospital; operational and privacy claims remain company-provided.
